learning_objectives: Surface what is already known about evidence assembly and portfolio completion without penalty and establish the unit question.

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Project work on evidence assembly and portfolio completion. Project: plan, select, sequence, document, test, and revise a sustained body of work through evidence assembly and portfolio completion, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision. Produce defensible evidence with intent, method, limitation, and revision traceable.
primary_task: Target for this probe session: Surface what is already known about evidence assembly and portfolio completion without penalty and establish the unit question. Communicate understanding of evidence assembly and portfolio completion using subject-appropriate evidence or representation. Check, revise, or improve the work on evidence assembly and portfolio completion against the stated success criteria. Closing evidence check: Name one thing you already understand about evidence assembly and portfolio completion and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit. 1. Diagnostic: Before instruction, make or analyse a brief first attempt involving evidence assembly and portfolio completion. Keep it unchanged; record three concrete noticings and one question. 2. Reflection: Compare an earlier and later state. Name the choice that changed, cite what became visible, audible, notated, or workable, and state the next revision or reason to keep the result. Your choices remain yours: Different project question, items to develop or select, private presentation format, sequence, revision and next-step priorities choices are valid when the learner meets objective constraints and supports the result with evidence. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about evidence assembly and portfolio completion, and it belongs to "Capstone Defense, Portfolio Completion, and Transition", which also covers separate topics such as artist statement final revision. Close out with this check before you stop: Name one thing you already understand about evidence assembly and portfolio completion and one thing you want resolved by the end of the unit. At grade 12 the bar is portfolio-quality independent work you could defend to an outside reader: intent stated, method justified, limitations named honestly, and revision traceable.

deliverable: Diagnostic, Reflection, with the observable Arts evidence and learner-owned decisions identified in each block.
critique_criteria: The submission contains an unchanged baseline; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.

The learner locates relevant purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.

The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, score excerpt, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting evidence assembly and portfolio completion.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or adult demonstration.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce evidence assembly and portfolio completion to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one purpose relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact purpose evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply evidence assembly and portfolio completion under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on evidence assembly and portfolio completion rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

arts_music_r1.learning_goal: Project: plan, select, sequence, document, test, and revise a sustained body of work through evidence assembly and portfolio completion, then use observable evidence to explain or revise a learner-owned decision.
arts_music_r1.prerequisite_summary: curation plus the ability to complete a short study, loop, observation, or plan without aiming for polish.

concept_registry.meaning: A portfolio or project is a purposeful sequence of work and decisions, not simply a pile of finished pieces.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one purpose relationship while working on evidence assembly and portfolio completion.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

age_policy.language: Portfolio-ready disciplinary language with limitations and decisions stated precisely.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

vocabulary.definition: a piece of work or process evidence
a bounded checkpoint with reviewable evidence

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for evidence assembly and portfolio completion is present, but the record does not yet locate purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
